Most people do it backwards. They build the system first, then go hunting for proof it works.

Alex Hormozi scaled a gym chain to six locations, walked away, and then spent roughly two years fixing other people's gyms by hand — more than 32 of them — before Gym Launch licensed anything at all.

The system he eventually sold was not designed in a room. It was the written-down version of something he had already done 32 times.

That order matters more than the content of the system. A framework built before the reps is a guess with a logo on it.

Do the reps. Then productise.
